scale.3: Fully satisfactory. Completeness: all task requirements met. Quality: correct, appropriately presented, free of misleading content.
scale.2: Mostly satisfactory. Completeness: at least 75% of the task requirements met. Quality: only minor deficiencies that do not affect the main conclusions.
scale.1: Partially satisfactory. Completeness: only part of the task addressed or essential requirements omitted. Quality: substantive errors (incorrect data or masking, conclusions inconsistent with the reference results or the reported numerical values).
scale.0: Unsatisfactory. Completeness: no valid output or output unrelated to the task. Quality: fundamentally incorrect or no evaluable result.

rules.completeness: Checked against the key questions of the query: every requested quantity is reported (presence only) and every interpretive item (why / whether / which / what it implies) is answered. A generic answer to a requested description counts as partly addressed.
rules.quality: Judged against the run's OWN reported numbers and established science, not against the reference numbers. 3 = interpretation consistent with its numbers and scientifically sound; 2 = minor errors in side statements, overstated claims or presentation slips, or wrong/self-contradicting answers to at most about one third of the query's explicitly required interpretive items; 1 = wrong or self-contradicting answers to more than about one third of the explicitly required interpretive items; 0 = no evaluable result (a run that finishes but yields no valid answer to any key question is scored like a crashed run).
rules.not_graded: Numerical accuracy (graded separately by src/eval/evaluate.py), and insights in the reference answer that the query does not ask for.
rules.repeats: Every completed run is scored on its own. In folders with repeats, per_task[T] is a list with one entry per scored run (repeat 1 = the first run of each task); summary means are the mean over tasks of the per-task mean over runs. Runs still in progress when the file was written are listed under not_scored.

T2.quality_note: 1 of the 2 required interpretive items is wrong: the explanation of why the El Nino counts differ (16 vs 22) is attributed to rounding, averaging conventions and event segmentation; the actual cause, ONI's periodically updated base period versus a fixed 1991-2020 baseline that makes earlier decades read cold, is missed. The offset agreement is read correctly.

T3.completeness_note: All quantities and the ranking reported, but the requested description of the spatial structure of the bias is generic ('regional departures remain') and names no region.
T3.quality_note: Interpretation consistent with its numbers; no incorrect statement.

T4.completeness_note: Ranking with criterion, regions (located extremes per model and month) and reasons all given.
T4.quality_note: Reason correct (displaced parcel at local pressure and monthly mean of instantaneous MLD versus operator on monthly-mean profiles).

T5.completeness_note: All items answered, including ratio meaningfulness and the CESM2 r1/r10 member caveat.
T5.quality_note: Ratio meaningfulness is wrong for GFDL-ESM4 and MPI ('meaningful' on member continuity, although their historical CIs include zero); CI judgements and the member caveat are right, so the wrong share does not exceed about one third. Also calls the ssp245 decline strongest in CESM2 while MPI's slope is larger.
